chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about separating the two witnesses in divorce, so he said, 'Yes, and she counts the waiting period from the first of the two witnesses.' And he said, 'It is not valid until both are testified to.' So there is no contradiction between this report and the first report, because his saying (peace be upon him) when asked about the validity of separating the two witnesses in divorce does not explicitly indicate that it is valid in the act of calling them to witness or in the act of testifying. And if that is not explicit, we interpret it as being valid in the act of testifying, and there is no contradiction between the two reports.

key_terms.الِاسْتِشْهَادِ: The act of testifying / obtaining testimony
key_terms.الْإِشْهَادِ: The act of calling to witness / summoning

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for witnesses to testify separately in a divorce case according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the juristic nuance of separating witness testimony in divorce is clarified: while the iddah countdown begins with the first witness, the legal validity of the divorce remains contingent upon the joint testimony of both. This resolves apparent contradictions in other reports by distinguishing between the procedural act of witnessing (ishhad) and the evidentiary act of testifying (ishtihad), a distinction central to Shia usul al-fiqh. The hadith underscores the precision required in applying evidentiary rules to ensure the sanctity and finality of marital dissolution.
